import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 43

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/43](https://www.erdosproblems.com/43)
-/

open scoped Pointwise

namespace Erdos43

/--
Let $f(N)$ be the maximum possible size of a Sidon set in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$.
-/
noncomputable abbrev f (N : ℕ) : ℕ := Finset.maxSidonSubsetCard (Finset.Icc 1 N)

/--
If $A$ and $B$ are Sidon sets in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ with
$(A-A)\cap(B-B)=\{0\}$, is it true that
$$\binom{\lvert A\rvert}{2}+\binom{\lvert B\rvert}{2}\leq\binom{f(N)}{2}+O(1)?$$

The answer is no; the Erdős Problems page notes that this follows from the solution to
Erdős Problem 42.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_43.parts.i : answer(False) ↔
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ᶠ N in Filter.atTop, ∀ (A B : Finset ℕ),
      A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N →
      B ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N →
      IsSidon (A : Set ℕ) →
      IsSidon (B : Set ℕ) →
      (A - A) ∩ (B - B) = {0} →
      ((A.card.choose 2 + B.card.choose 2 : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ ((f N).choose 2 : ℝ) + C := by
  sorry

/--
If $A$ and $B$ are equal-sized Sidon sets in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ with
$(A-A)\cap(B-B)=\{0\}$, can the bound be improved to
$$\binom{\lvert A\rvert}{2}+\binom{\lvert B\rvert}{2}
    \leq (1-c+o(1))\binom{f(N)}{2}$$
for some constant $c>0$?

The answer is no; the Erdős Problems page records a negative answer due to Barreto.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_43.parts.ii : answer(False) ↔
    ∃ᵉ (c > 0), ∃ o : ℕ → ℝ, o =o[Filter.atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ) ∧
    ∀ᶠ N in Filter.atTop, ∀ (A B : Finset ℕ),
      A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N →
      B ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N →
      IsSidon (A : Set ℕ) →
      IsSidon (B : Set ℕ) →
      A.card = B.card →
      (A - A) ∩ (B - B) = {0} →
      ((A.card.choose 2 + B.card.choose 2 : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤
        (1 - c + o N) * ((f N).choose 2 : ℝ) := by
  sorry

end Erdos43

reformulations.difference: The difference-set hypothesis uses truncated subtraction on ℕ rather than signed integer differences.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For positive d, membership in a natural-number self-difference set is equivalent to membership of its integer cast in the corresponding signed difference set. Signed self-difference sets are symmetric, so a common negative difference also gives a common positive difference. Zero belongs to both self-difference sets exactly when both original sets are nonempty. Consequently the intersection equals {0} in ℕ iff it equals {0} after embedding the sets into ℤ, including empty-set cases. This exact equivalence is proved by nat_sub_inter_eq_zero_iff_int in the scratch file.

reformulations.difference: As in part (i), the common-difference condition is expressed using natural-number subtraction.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The same proved equivalence applies to every pair of finite natural-number sets, independently of their Sidon properties or equal cardinalities. Replacing this hypothesis with signed integer differences therefore leaves the equal-sized, asymptotic-gap question unchanged.

review.notes: Checked all three declarations. The definition f is the attained maximum cardinality of a Sidon subset of {1,…,N}. Both statements have the correct uniform asymptotic quantifiers, real-valued constants, inequalities, and answer polarity. Both solved tags agree with the source. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, I proved maximum attainment and its upper-bound property, the subtraction equivalence, little-o-of-one equivalence to convergence to zero, and satisfiability of the hypotheses for every N≥1; I also evaluated f and exhaustively checked admissible pairs for N=0,…,9. The scratch file compiles without errors or warnings, and the subtraction proof has no sorry dependency. The live source returned a Cloudflare challenge, so I used archived official pages and the currently retrieved status database. No repository files were edited.
